notable.report:
YS390906:AT LOC STATED, D COY 8 RAR CONTACTED A PL TP COYSIZE EN  FORCE WHO FIRED SA/AW AND RPG 2. 10 PL D COY8 RAR WERE FIRST CON BY 2 EN IN A WELL CONSTRUCTED TRENCH RESULTINGIN ONE AUST WIA. THE REMAINDER OF THE PL WITHDREW AND WHILE ATTEMpTINGTO RECOVER WIA, PL CAME UNDER HEAVY SA FIRE FROM A BUNKER SYSTEM RESULTING ON ONE AUST KIA. AT H THIS TIME ANOTHER PL WASDEPLOYED TO ASSIST IN THE CONTACT RESULTING IN A FURTHER AUST WIA. BUSHRANGERS (LFT) AND ARTY WERE USED IN SUPPORT OF THECONTACT. THE KIA AND WEAPON WERE RECOVERED AND D COY WITHDREW EAST.RES: ONE AUST KIA. 2 AUST WIA NIL EN CASUaLTIES. 

Intsum 22/12/69: D Coy 8 RAR enters the bunker system and finds 1 dead enemy and an AK47.


30-40 well trained enemy were occupying 6 bunkers when they were discovered by D coy. The enemy opened fire wounding an engineer (GSW to right thigh and buttock). Supported by 11 pl , 10 pl assaulted the bunkers and after 2hrs 40 minutes, had rendered 1 bunker ineffective and repulsed an enemy counter attack. 2 further Aust cas. 1 soldier shot in chest and killed, 1 soldier with graze to head. Dusk forced a break in action but D coy returned the next day with tanks. The enemy withdrew before the arrival of the tanks. Enemy losses were 1 killed and 1 wounded for certain, but probably his losses were higher.

161 Fd Bty fired in support. (AWM95 3/6/21.pdf p17 1 Fd Regt Diary)

units: 10 Platoon, D Company, 8 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
The patrol contacted 11 enemy and killed 8 and captured 2 wded. M60 and claymores used initially. The ambush was covering a track junction near the Suoi Hoa Nuoc next to paddi fields. At approx 2055hrs the sentry on the M60 heard a radio playing and waited until it was in the killing area. The Claymores were fired and M60 and M79 were fired into the arc of the killing ground. After 5 mins firing ceased and moaning was heard. 2xM79 flares were fired and M26 and M79 HE was fired in a systematic neutralising pattern for 10 mins. Arty was called in (161 Fd Bty) and registered 600m W of ambush position. Capt 1 RPG2, 2xM1 Carbines, 1xAK47, 1xSKS, 2xpistols, 4 grenades.

The patrol OC observed that fire must be directed low to the ground with the arcs of fire interlocking. All of the killing group must give maximum fire to the killing area once ambush is sprung.

Intsum 14/1/70 reports that a patrol from D Coy contacted 11 enemy. 8 enemy were killed including 1 female, and 2 wded VC were captured. 1 RPG-2, 1xM1 Garrand, 2xM1, 1xSKS, 2xpistol, 1xAK47, 4 grenades were captured.

units: 2 Troop, 1 Armoured Regiment
9 Platoon, C Company, 8 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
YS458564, 9/C/8RAR CON AN EST COY MOVING N RESULTING IN 7 ENKIA (BC). A SWEEP ON THE MORNING OF 16/02/70 RESULTED IN 2 SMALLCONTACTS RESULTING IN 2 EN KIA (BC)(see 16/02/70 1200hrs). A FURTHER BODY WAS ALSO LOC.RES: 10 EN KIA (BC), 22 DRAG MARKS (22 EN KIA/WIA POSS), 1 AK47,1 M16, 1 M2, 1 PISTOL (NFI), QTY OF DOCUS AND MANY ASSTD GRENS CIA.

During the action the enemy counter attacked. With the 9 pl running low on ammo, 2 Tp 1 Armd Regt was scrambled from FSPB Isa, joined up with 8 pl at 455568  and rescued the infantry, staying with them all night. While in contact with the 100+ enemy.  9 pl received 155mm arty and 2xHFT support. A heavy exchange of fire continued until1957 and sporadic fire until 2047hrs.

Arty support was: B/2/13 US Arty fired on grid YS469569, later 161 Fd Bty fired on YS443563, the Dat Do 155s engaged YS460546, A/7/8 US Arty engaged YS455560 and YS421542  (AWM95 3/6/23.pdf p10 1 Fd Regt Diary)

The area of the ambush was chosen because it was thought possible to ambush a large enemy force. Everything was planned carefully. The pl was inserted by tanks, 1000m from the ambush site. The tanks moved off and created a diversion by firing, while the pl quietly moved in undetected with engineers checking for mines in the site, and with FO and MFC for close arty and mor support. The tanks returned to FSPB ISA where they would come and support the pl if needed. 15 claymores were sighted for maximum effect along a track.
The pl was occupying its ambush positions when the 1st of 4 enemy groups (28 men ) were allowed to pass through. The second and third groups were hit by different banks of claymores and appear to have been wiped out for no further reaction came from these areas. The 1st and 4th enemy groups tried to sort out where the pl was and to counter attack. They were met by heavy SA fire including M72 and M79 fire. 3 Aust were wounded and were dusted off during the firefight. After 10 mins mortar fire began to support the pl and to cut-off enemy retreat routes. Arty support followed soon after. The pl was resupplied twice with first line ammo. Within 40 mins the tanks arrived and cleared the killing ground by fire. The tanks remained and provided illumination and interdictory fire throughout the night.

Not possible to accurately assign enemy cas to particular weapons. It has been estimated. Bob has detailed Contact report of this action.

notable.report:
YS475523, C/8RAR AND ELMS B/3 CAV REGT AND A/1 ARMD REGT CON EST 40 EN WHO FIRED RPG2'S. RES: 1 APC DES, 2 AUST KIA [Hugh Carlyle of 3 Cav], 7 AUST WIA,1 VC KIA (BC), AND 1 PW CAPTURED. 

Initial contact was made 1045hrs YS475522 with 3 VC and HQ C Coy. 1 VC was captured and revealed that 40 enemy were a short distance away in a bunker system and that there were many anti personnel mines in the area.
 Full company attack was launched on located bunker system, with APC and tank support resulting in 1 APC being destroyed by 2 RPGs, 2 men killed and over 7 wounded. The Coy withdrew and arty and air strikes were launched. At 1300hrs C coy attacked again with tank troop leading. This assault fought through the bunker system against little significant opposition but on reaching the far side of the bunker system found that further progress was impeded by a deep creek (YS475532). 

At this point the assaulting force was advised that  as well as anti-personnel mines and booby traps, the bunker system also was protected by an anti-tank minefield. While the OC considered whether to dismount the infantry, orders were received to break contact and withdraw. 

While withdrawing (1430hrs)  the assault force again came under heavy fire from RPGs and SA from enemy who had re-occupied the bunkers. 1 Aust wounded. At 1500hrs (YS475543) 5 more Aust were wounded by shrapnel. The assault force withdrew and contact was broken at approx 1520 hrs. Air and artillery fire was then brought to bear on the bunker system until 1830 hrs. At this time a further assault was made by tanks and the HQ APC Tp to recover the APC casualty. This was successfully done by 1900 hrs when the final break with the enemy was made and the contact ended. 8RAR did not return to the bunker system till the morning of 20 February after a B52 strike had been brought down upon the position. During the contact 12 enemy were killed and many blood trails indicating many wounded were found. The system was extensive and was defended by 30-40 enemy (also described as 1 Bn of enemy). 1 tank was hit 8 times by RPGs but remained in action. Another APC was also hit by RPGs.  Most of the enemy cas were caused by tank cannister and HE rds.

A/7/8 US Arty, B/2/13 US Arty and the 155mm of Dat Do fired in support of C Coy 8 RAR (AWM95 3/6/23.pdf p11 1 Fd Regt Diary)

YS455546, 6/B/8RAR AND ELMS B/3 CAV CON 1 VC WHO ENG APC WITHRPG2. RES: 1 APC DAM, 3 AUST WIA.

While travelling down jungle trail to an ambush position, 2 section was ambushed by an RPG2 team which hit twice, the leading APC penetrating the hull and wounding the two crew. The damaged APC was driven to a more secure area, and the enemy dispersed by APC counter fire (0.30). Enemy also fired AK47s. 5 pl who were nearby 200m, having been concentrating for the APCs to pick them up for a move), put in a quick sweep, finding nothing, They then secured the LZ for cas evac. The enemy came from a nearby bunker system not known about at the time.

Following the C Coy 8 RAR heavy contact, B Coy was being hurried into blocking positions by APC. 4 pl had just dismounted and were moving forward with the APCs in support when 3 section was fired on by the enemy. Receiving heavy SA fire, RPGs were fired at the APCs, one hitting an APC on the left side. The two crew were injured and the hull was punctured. Heavy fire was poured into the area. A sweep was organised when enemy fire subsided, but 10m into the jungle claymore type wires were noticed, and the pl was pulled back. The 8 Aust cas were caused by RPGs.

YS475585, 3/A/8RAR CON 40-50 VC CARRYING AK47'S RPG'S MGS ANDM79'S. EN WERE MOV N-S. AFTER INITIAL CON EN WDR AND REORG ANDRECOVERED THEIR KIA BY FIRE AND MOVT. EN WDR S. SWEEP OF AREAREVEALED 3 BT AND DRAG MARKS LEADING S. RES: 2 VC KIA, 1 M16 AND1 M26 RECOVERED, 6 AUST WIA.

See Combat Battalion pg131-7

After the initial ambush the enemy counter attacked. After one hours fighting 3 Tp was summoned to assist the infantry. It arrived at about 2120hrs and at 2130hrs the enemy broke contact.

Intel later claimed over 50 enemy killed.

Pl was moving to AP when contact was started when the lead sect saw and fired on the enemy. The pl closed into a fire base. En returned fire with AK47s, RPG-7, M79, RPD, M16, and M26. Other en parties moved to other flank and engaged pl position. En withdrew reorged and using fire and movement, moved to within 10m of pl position to recover their wounded and some of their dead. The 6 friendly cas were caused by RPG and M26.

notable.report:
AT YS402633 8/C/8RAR AND 1/B/3 CAV REGT AMBUSHED 50-60 VCLEAVING HOA LONG IN 2 GPS 50M APART. RES: 19 VC KIA (BC), 6 VC PW,1 HOI CHANH. CIA: 2 AK47, 3 M1 CARBINES, 1 M79, 2 7.62 SMG,1 M26 GREN, AMMO FOR ALL WPNS, QTY DOCUS, 50 TORCH BATTERIES, LGEQTY CLOTHING, 72LB SUGAR, LGE QTY TOBACCO, 10LB SALT, 65LB OTHERFRESH FOOD, 220 TINS FOOD, 100LB RICE CAKES, 550LB RICE. SURVIVORSWDR SE. (PART SERIAL A286 ONLY).

8pl was ambushing and observed the enemy entering the village at 2100hrs 11 Aug. It decided to wait and ambush the enemy as they retired later in the night. 1 Tp was put on alert to assist as soon as the ambush was sprung. This happened at 315hrs 12 Aug. The enemy immediately counter attacked the platoon but retreated as soon as the APCs arrived. The APCs pursued the enemy killing one and capturing 5. The Tp stayed with the pl until dawn.

The original task of the pl was to ambush Route 2 because this was thought to be a supply route into Hoa Long. At 2050hrs, the W gps of the ambush observed 50-60 en moving along the paddi bunds. The en moved carefully with 20m separating each man and they crouched low to avoid silhouette. Since the en were not going to go into the AP killing ground, the decision was made to let them pass and shift the ambush to meet the en on their return later that night.

The en returned at 315hrs moving in 2 gps of 25 with spacing of only 2-3m and the distance between the 2 gps was 20-30m. They were carrying packs and were not nearly so alert as for the move in. The en came straight towards gp 3 so the ambush had to be initiated before the main body was in the killing ground. Claymores were fired, and although the en were not in the killing ground, a good crossfire was achieved from all 4 MGs. The majority of en cas were inflicted by SA, but M72s were also used to good effect from gp 4. All of the first en gp were killed or wounded. The second en gp withdrew to the SE, taking the wounded of the 1 st with them. Very little return fire was received. Arty and mors fired for illum and to block escape routes.

A quick response from 1 Tp 3 CAV allowed the ambush to be exploited gaining 2 en killed and 5 POW who had hidden in the scrub about 800m from the ambush.
